related_questions.question: How much money can you have in the bank and still get food stamps in ny?

text_blocks.snippet: In New York, most households applying for SNAP (food stamps) benefits are no longer subject to a resource limit, meaning the amount of money you have in a bank account or other assets generally won't affect your eligibility. Specifically, the state eliminated the asset test for SNAP as of January 1, 2008. However, there are exceptions for elderly or disabled individuals.
snippet_highlighted_words: most households applying for SNAP (food stamps) benefits are no longer subject to a resource limit

list.title: General Rule:
list.snippet: For most households, the amount of money in savings, checking, or retirement accounts does not impact SNAP eligibility, as long as they meet the income guidelines.

list.title: Elderly or Disabled Individuals:
list.snippet: Households with at least one member aged 60 or older, or with a disability, may have up to $3,000 in countable resources (like cash or bank accounts) and still be eligible for SNAP, or $4,500 if they are over the age of 60 or disabled and do not meet the gross income limit.

list.title: Expedited SNAP Benefits:
list.snippet: If your monthly income and cash on hand are less than your rent/mortgage and utilities combined, you may be eligible for expedited SNAP benefits, potentially receiving them within seven days.

list.title: Income Limits:
list.snippet: While asset limits are largely eliminated, income limits still apply.

list.title: Documentation:
list.snippet: When applying for SNAP, you will need to provide documentation of your income and household size, and some states may also require you to provide information about your assets, according to Propel.

related_questions.question: How often do you have to recertify for SNAP in ny?

text_blocks.snippet: In New York, SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) recipients generally need to recertify their eligibility every 6 to 12 months. The exact recertification period depends on the specific circumstances of the household. For example, households with income that changes frequently may have a 6-month recertification period, while most households with income and those with no income have a 12-month period. Some households, like those in the Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP), may have a 36-month period.

To recertify, you'll need to complete a recertification form, provide any required documentation, and attend an interview if requested. It's crucial to recertify on time to avoid a gap in benefits. The New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA) will notify you about the recertification process and any required actions.
